title: Physical implications of a $1$-dimensional base
html:
Remark. Physical implications of a 1-dimensional base

At dimension 1, the physical content simplifies drastically.

  1. Primordial vortex. The vortex filaments of the mass identity are no longer embedded in a larger space. The entire manifold is the filament.

  2. Mass as pure drag. When \dim M_k = 1, the surface \Sigma in the mass identity degenerates to the 1-manifold M_k itself. The 2-dimensional nonabelian multiplicative integral reduces, via the nonabelian Stokes theorem [yekutieli2015], to the holonomy of the connection \nabla_A around M_k:

      m = 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}\!\bigl(M_k; \mathfrak{G}\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert.

    Mass thereby represents the fundamental holonomy resistance of the 1-dimensional flow against the \mathrm{SU}(2) rotation.

  3. Lepton generations. Because the Euler characteristic and vertical degree bound the number of lepton generations (Betti numbers on branes), a 1-dimensional base supports only the most fundamental fermionic state. It leaves no room for higher-degree vertical harmonic forms.
